look/keep: A plain decoder only sees the encoder's final state. Attention keeps all of them: one state per input word, here for je, suis, and étudiant.
look/score: At each step, the decoder scores every encoder state against its own state, q. A simple score is the dot product: two, zero, and one.
look/weights: Softmax turns the scores into weights that are positive and add up to one: zero point six seven, zero point zero nine, and zero point two four.
look/context: The context vector is the weighted sum of the states: mostly je, a little of the rest. Here, one point five eight and zero point zero nine.
look/use: The decoder reads this context along with its own state to predict the next word: I.
every/again: At the next step the decoder's state has moved on, so the scores change, and it looks somewhere else: for am and a, at suis; for student, at étudiant.
every/grid: Stack the weights, one row per output word, and they show which input words each output word drew on.
every/free: Nothing has to squeeze through one fixed-size vector any more: every step can read every input state directly. That is attention.
